question: Are TRAVEL-READ's one-cross-section window bonds real (certified by doubly periodic or eventually periodic states, minimal in a twice-larger window), and do the bounded bases stay bounded far away and around rank-2 bases?

definitions.inputs: TRAVEL-READ cross.jsonl (sha256 a64cf9596c5099ab5bf9b4fb96e7a526b6060183cc6e38c5b64f43f84917e70c), dirs.jsonl (sha256 6ec375b4c6a6d5e19256ba0ae3a412240749abf76e8db866896d74ddce660596), rings.jsonl (sha256 00723264b96d4e33c0e17ab8e2b40bdc36fdd3b145dd63c326a61780df4b75b9); its census.py (sha256 c59ca676b7b91cf923efcd1293d099de9bdf30841643f9323741505ef4f6b2ca)
definitions.certified bond: refuted on the frame window, every proper part carried in every pattern by a doubly periodic or an eventually periodic state (P >= the kinds' largest along-span)
definitions.classes: bounded across / growing across / unresolved on b_cert, as in census.py

public_inputs.run: --part control, recheck, far, rings; outputs in artifacts/FAR-BOUND-20261112-001A/FAR-BOUND-20261112-001A-E001_bounded_far/

forbidden_inputs: Changing targets, windows, certificates, caps or predictions after seeing results
primary_observable: Per base the class on certified bonds, near and far b_cert and b_win; ring statistics
cheapest_meaningful_control: Base 16 (part control): its theorem's profile certified

predictions.F1: >= 40 of 66 rank-1 bases bounded across on certified bonds
predictions.F2: on >= 2/3 of bounded bases, far b_cert <= max near b_cert + 1 wherever defined and >= 80% of far targets with a certified bond
predictions.F3: on >= 2/3 of rank-2 bases, >= 80% of ring-15 targets with a bond <= 5 and max <= TRAVEL-READ ring-3 max + 1

decision_rules.headline: TRAVEL-READ's 56 of 66 corrected (Narrowing) if fewer than 56 certified-bounded, overturned below 33

stop_rule: One run of each part; hand-off to the referee thread.
runtime: About 2 hours in all on 6 + 4 workers; each base saved as it finishes; 1,800 s cap per base.
